pos.personaBrief: Paisley's Liverpool built patiently from the back and valued not giving the ball away, but also switched to counters in three or four passes (These Football Times, SI, 1983 quote on patience).

pro.personaBrief: He said Liverpool learned to be patient after winning the ball and play out ('no use winning the ball if you finished on your backside'), though the 'right ball' can be long.

est.personaBrief: Players were trusted to read the game: full-backs overlapped with cover, Dalglish dropped deep, and tactical coaching was kept to a minimum.

lar.personaBrief: Wingers delivered first-time service and diagonals into space, but the 4-4-2 with Dalglish and a passing accent was mixed, not purely wing-based.

blo.personaBrief: The blocks moved in territorial unison with a high line and pressing up to the halfway line, defending and attacking together.

mar.personaBrief: No marking evidence; the compact collective 'Liverpool Way' with zonal-style unison suggests space-oriented defending, inferred weakly.

pla.personaBrief: Rarely set up specifically against opponents; first instinct was the natural game, with in-game tweaks, and his 1977 quote that tactics were unstoppable despite being predictable.

res.personaBrief: Obsessed with trophies ('we never celebrate second place'), though the football was fluent; he valued winning over how.

sis.personaBrief: He judged players and fit them to a basic system, with minimal tactical coaching, expecting intelligent players to read the game; everyone worked and ran.

jog.personaBrief: He wanted defenders able to bring the ball out and passing over distance, with technique, plus relentless running and work rate.

bas.personaBrief: Nucleus experienced and not too old, new signings eased in slowly, gradual change, a few youngsters; signings like Dalglish, Souness, Rush.

lid.personaBrief: A quiet, calm man-manager who spoke softly and aired views in the Boot Room, yet ruthlessly moved players on and removed the captaincy.
